20	// TestExitErrorForStatus guards the exit-code contract between this agent and
21	// the executor that watches its Job.
22	//
23	// The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded in
24	// agent-task-executor's job_watcher) and never reads the Status this agent
25	// publishes. So a run that reports failure but exits 0 is written as a phase
26	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at
27	// human_review as though a human had parked it deliberately.
28	//
29	// Observed 2026-11-03: task ceb79961 published Status=failed for
30	// "git clone --bare: Failed to connect to github.com port 443", exited 0, and
31	// parked at human_review.
32	func TestExitErrorForStatus(t *testing.T) {
33		ctx := context.Background()
34		phase := domain.TaskPhase("execution")
35	
36		cases := []struct {
37			name    string
38			status  agentlib.AgentStatus
39			wantErr bool
40		}{
41			{
42				name:    "failed must fail the Job so the executor does not record a phase success",
43				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusFailed,
44				wantErr: true,
45			},
46			{
47				name:    "done exits 0",
48				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusDone,
49				wantErr: false,
50			},
51			{
52				name:    "in_progress exits 0",
53				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusInProgress,
54				wantErr: false,
55			},
56			{
57				// needs_input reaches the same park path on purpose: the task is meant
58				// to wait at human_review for an answer, not to be re-driven.
59				name:    "needs_input exits 0 — parking for a human answer is its intent",
60				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusNeedsInput,
61				wantErr: false,
62			},
63		}
64	
65		for _, c := range cases {
66			t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
67				err := exitErrorForStatus(ctx, c.status, phase)
68				if c.wantErr && err == nil {
69					t.Fatalf(
70						"status %q: expected a non-nil error, got nil — the Job would exit 0 and the executor would record it as a phase success",
71						c.status,
72					)
73				}
74				if !c.wantErr && err != nil {
75					t.Fatalf("status %q: expected nil, got %v", c.status, err)
76				}
77			})
78		}
79	}
80	
81	// TestPrintRedactsAnthropicAuthToken guards the startup argument dump against
82	// republishing the ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN value into the Job log.
83	//
84	// argument.Print honours only display:"hidden" and display:"length"; every other
85	// tag value falls through to the plaintext branch (`Argument: %s '%v'`). The root
86	// binary's application struct carried display:"password" — a value the printer does
87	// not implement — so each Job start wrote the live model-router credential in
88	// cleartext. This test drives the real printer over the real struct, so removing
89	// the display:"length" tag turns it red.
90	//
91	// Plain testing rather than Ginkgo on purpose: application is unexported, so the
92	// assertion must live in package main, and package main_test (main_test.go) shares
93	// this test binary — where a second RunSpecs fails with "calling RunSpecs more than
94	// once". An internal spec therefore cannot join the existing suite. Same shape as
95	// TestExitErrorForStatus above.
96	func TestPrintRedactsAnthropicAuthToken(t *testing.T) {
97		const sentinel = "sentinel-token-do-not-log-9f3a2b7c1d"
98	
99		var buf bytes.Buffer
100		log.SetOutput(&buf)
101		log.SetFlags(0)
102		defer func() {
103			log.SetOutput(os.Stderr)
104			log.SetFlags(log.LstdFlags)
105		}()
106	
107		if err := argument.Print(context.Background(), &application{AnthropicAuthToken: sentinel}); err != nil {
108			t.Fatalf("print: %v", err)
109		}
110	
111		rendered := buf.String()
112		if got := strings.Count(rendered, sentinel); got != 0 {
113			t.Fatalf(
114				"token value leaked into the argument dump: sentinel appeared %d times\n%s",
115				got,
116				rendered,
117			)
118		}
119		if got := strings.Count(rendered, "AnthropicAuthToken"); got != 1 {
120			t.Fatalf("want the field named exactly once, got %d\n%s", got, rendered)
121		}
122		if !strings.Contains(rendered, "Argument: AnthropicAuthToken length ") {
123			t.Fatalf("want the length form, got:\n%s", rendered)
124		}
125	}

120	func (a *application) Run(ctx context.Context, _ libsentry.Client) error {
121		registry := prometheus.NewRegistry()
122		jobMetrics := libmetrics.NewJobMetrics(registry, libtime.NewCurrentDateTime())

124			Grouping("agent", agentName).
125			Grouping("task_type", a.TaskType).
126			Collector(registry)
127		defer func() {
128			if err := pusher.PushContext(ctx); err != nil {
129				glog.Warningf("prometheus push failed: %v", err)

131			}
132			glog.V(2).Infof("prometheus push completed")
133		}()
134		start := libtime.NewCurrentDateTime().Now().Time()
135	
136		glog.V(2).Infof("github-dark-factory-agent started phase=%s", a.Phase)
137	
138		// Resolve the GitHub credential (App IAT or raw GH_TOKEN fallback) and make
139		// it usable by every git/gh subprocess. See prepareAuth.
140		resolvedToken, err := a.prepareAuth(ctx)

142			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)

147		deliverer := delivery.NewNoopResultDeliverer()
148		if a.TaskID != "" {

150				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)

153			}

155			if err != nil {
156				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
157				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
158				return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "create sync producer")
159			}
160			defer func() {
161				if err := syncProducer.Close(); err != nil {
162					glog.Warningf("close sync producer failed: %v", err)
163				}
164			}()
165			deliverer = factory.CreateKafkaResultDeliverer(
166				syncProducer, a.TopicPrefix, a.TaskID, a.TaskContent,
167				libtime.NewCurrentDateTime(),
168			)
169		}
170	
171		claudeEnv := a.buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken)
172	
173		repoManager := factory.CreateRepoManager(a.ReposPath, a.WorkPath, resolvedToken)
174		githubClient := factory.CreateGitHubClient(resolvedToken)
175		claudeProber := factory.CreateClaudeProber(a.ClaudeConfigDir)
176		provider := factory.CreateAgentProvider(
177			a.ClaudeConfigDir,
178			a.AgentDir,
179			a.AnthropicModel,
180			resolvedToken,
181			claudeEnv,
182			repoManager,
183			githubClient,
184			claudeProber,
185			// Re-mint before the push: the installation token is minted once here at
186			// startup and expires after 60 minutes, but a lifecycle run routinely
187			// takes longer, so the final push would be refused as an invalid token.
188			a.resolveAuth,
189		)
190		agent, err := provider.Get(ctx, agentlib.TaskType(a.TaskType))
191		if err != nil {
192			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
193			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
194			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "select agent for task_type")
195		}
196	
197		result, err := agent.Run(ctx, a.Phase, a.TaskContent, deliverer)
198		if err != nil {
199			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
200			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
201			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "agent run failed")
202		}
203		jobMetrics.RecordRun(result.Status)
204		jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
205		return finishRun(ctx, result, a.Phase)
206	}
207	
208	// finishRun publishes the agent's result and then decides the Job's exit code.
209	// It exists as one call so Run stays within its funlen budget.
210	func finishRun(
211		ctx context.Context,
212		result *agentlib.Result,
213		phase domain.TaskPhase,
214	) error {
215		if err := agentlib.PrintResult(ctx, result); err != nil {
216			return err
217		}
218		return exitErrorForStatus(ctx, result.Status, phase)
219	}
220	
221	// exitErrorForStatus returns a non-nil error when the agent's published status
222	// must fail the Job, and nil when the Job may exit 0.
223	//
224	// A failed result is still published to the task, but the Job must also exit
225	// non-zero. The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded
226	// in agent-task-executor's job_watcher), so returning nil here makes a failed run
227	// indistinguishable from a completed one: the failure is written as a phase
228	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at human_review
229	// as though a human had parked it deliberately (2026-11-03, task ceb79961: a Job
230	// that published Status=failed for a git clone error exited 0 and parked the
231	// task).
232	//
233	// needs_input is deliberately NOT a failure: parking for a human answer is that
234	// status's intent, and it reaches the same park path on purpose.
235	func exitErrorForStatus(
236		ctx context.Context,
237		status agentlib.AgentStatus,
238		phase domain.TaskPhase,
239	) error {
240		if status == agentlib.AgentStatusFailed {
241			return errors.Errorf(
242				ctx,
243				"agent reported status %q for phase %q",
244				status,
245				phase,
246			)
247		}
248		return nil
249	}
250	
251	// buildClaudeEnv assembles the Claude CLI subprocess env from the raw env
252	// pairs plus the Anthropic provider-routing overrides. resolvedToken, when
253	// non-empty, is threaded in as GH_TOKEN — the ai_review phase's Claude
254	// subprocess shells `gh pr view/diff`, and the runner strips pod env to an
255	// allowlist, so the token must be passed explicitly (os.Setenv in prepareAuth
256	// covers the dark-factory daemon path, not the Claude runner).
257	func (a *application) buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken string) map[string]string {
258		claudeEnv := envparse.KeyValuePairs(a.ClaudeEnvRaw)
259		if claudeEnv == nil {
260			claudeEnv = map[string]string{}
261		}
262		if a.AnthropicBaseURL != "" {
263			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"] = a.AnthropicBaseURL
264		}
265		if a.AnthropicAuthToken != "" {
266			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"] = a.AnthropicAuthToken
267		}
268		if a.AnthropicModel != "" {
269			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_MODEL"] = a.AnthropicModel.String()
270		}
271		if resolvedToken != "" {
272			claudeEnv["GH_TOKEN"] = resolvedToken
273		}
274		return claudeEnv
275	}
276	
277	// prepareAuth resolves the GitHub credential and makes it usable by every
278	// git/gh subprocess: it exports GH_TOKEN (covering the dark-factory daemon,
279	// which inherits os.Environ() for its `git push`) and installs git's credential
280	// helper via `gh auth setup-git`. Returns the resolved token for the
281	// RepoManager / GitHub client / gh-token preflight wiring.
282	func (a *application) prepareAuth(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
283		resolvedToken, err := a.resolveAuth(ctx)
284		if err != nil {
285			return "", err
286		}
287		// resolvedToken is always non-empty here (resolveAuth errors otherwise), but
288		// guard defensively — an empty GH_TOKEN would mislead the daemon subprocess.
289		if resolvedToken != "" {
290			if err := os.Setenv("GH_TOKEN", resolvedToken); err != nil {
291				return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "export GH_TOKEN")
292			}
293		}
294		if err := githubauth.NewGhAuthSetupGit(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
295			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "gh auth setup-git")
296		}
297		// A file the daemon re-reads outlives the token bound into gh's helper: the
298		// installation token expires after 60 minutes and the lifecycle daemon keeps
299		// its startup environment, so a long run's own `git fetch` would use a dead
300		// token (2026-11-03, bborbe/trading#433).
301		if err := githubauth.NewFileBackedHelper(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
302			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "configure file-backed credential helper")
303		}
304		return resolvedToken, nil
305	}
306	
307	// resolveAuth resolves the GitHub credential forwarded to every git/gh
308	// subprocess. It prefers GitHub App authentication: when APP_ID,
309	// INSTALLATION_ID, and a PEM (file or inline) are all set, it mints a
310	// short-lived installation access token via githubapp.MintIAT. Otherwise it
311	// falls back to the raw GH_TOKEN input — the local cmd/run-task path where the
312	// operator exports `gh auth token`. When neither is configured it returns a
313	// clear error, since the agent cannot clone or push without a credential.
314	//
315	// The token is a runtime value (not a config input), so it is returned to the
316	// caller rather than stored on the argument-parsed application struct —
317	// argument/v2 panics when reflecting over unexported struct fields at startup.
318	func (a *application) resolveAuth(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
319		hasPEMFile := a.PEMKeyFile != ""
320		hasPEMContent := a.PEMKey != ""
321		useGitHubApp := a.AppID != 0 && a.InstallationID != 0 && (hasPEMFile || hasPEMContent)
322		if useGitHubApp {
323			appCfg := githubapp.Config{AppID: a.AppID, InstallationID: a.InstallationID}
324			if hasPEMFile {
325				appCfg.PEMPath = a.PEMKeyFile
326			} else {
327				appCfg.PEM = []byte(a.PEMKey)
328			}
329			// Startup auth must not be killed by the task's work deadline: mint on a
330			// fresh bounded context (keeps ctx values, drops the caller's
331			// deadline/cancel) so a near-deadline task can't fail the token mint.
332			mintCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 30*time.Second)
333			defer cancel()
334			iat, err := githubapp.MintIAT(mintCtx, appCfg)
335			if err != nil {
336				return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "mint github app iat")
337			}
338			glog.V(2).Infof(
339				"github-dark-factory-agent auth mode=github-app app_id=%d installation_id=%d",
340				a.AppID, a.InstallationID,
341			)
342			return iat, nil
343		}
344		if a.GhToken != "" {
345			glog.V(2).Infof("github-dark-factory-agent auth mode=gh-token (raw GH_TOKEN fallback)")
346			return a.GhToken, nil
347		}
348		return "", errors.Errorf(
349			ctx,
350			"github-dark-factory-agent auth: no credentials configured — set GitHub App creds (APP_ID, INSTALLATION_ID, PEM_KEY_FILE or PEM_KEY) or GH_TOKEN",
351		)
352	}

# Definition of Done

The validation prompt dark-factory runs against each executed prompt before it
marks the prompt complete. A change is Done only when every box holds.

- [ ] Builds: `make precommit` exits 0 (generate + format + test + lint + vet + gosec + coverage).
- [ ] Tests: new/changed behavior has Ginkgo coverage; boundaries are mocked (counterfeiter), the framework Agent is not.
- [ ] Scope: the diff touches only what the spec asked for; no unrelated files.
- [ ] Errors: wrapped via `github.com/bborbe/errors`; no bare `return err`, no `fmt.Errorf`.
- [ ] Escalation doctrine: failure paths return `Status: failed`/`needs_input` without mutating `assignee`/`status` or writing a `## Failure` section.
- [ ] Docs: user-facing behavior changes are reflected in `docs/` and the CHANGELOG `## Unreleased` section.

11	// Step is one unit of work within a phase. Always code; may wrap AI calls.
12	//
13	// Three responsibilities:
14	//   - Name: identifies the step in logs and tests.
15	//   - ShouldRun: cheap guard that inspects task state to decide skip vs run.
16	//   - Run: performs work, mutating markdown in-place. Returns a Result
17	//     describing status + phase transition (NOT body content — body changes
18	//     happen via markdown.AddSection / ReplaceSection / Frontmatter mutation).
19	type Step interface {
20		// Name identifies the step. Convention: lower-kebab-case.
21		Name() string
22	
23		// ShouldRun returns true if the step should execute. Inspects markdown
24		// state (frontmatter, sections) and returns false if the step has
25		// already completed (idempotency guard).
26		//
27		// Guards must be cheap — no expensive I/O. Use existing markdown state.
28		ShouldRun(ctx context.Context, md *Markdown) (bool, error)
29	
30		// Run performs the step's work, mutating markdown in-place. Returns a
31		// Result describing status + phase transition. Body content changes
32		// flow through markdown.AddSection / ReplaceSection; frontmatter
33		// changes flow through direct map mutation.
34		//
35		// The framework re-serializes markdown via Marshal after Run returns
36		// and publishes the new content via the deliverer.
37		Run(ctx context.Context, md *Markdown) (*Result, error)
38	}
39	
40	// Result tells the StepRunner what status to deliver and whether to advance.
41	//
42	// Body and frontmatter changes are NOT in Result — they're applied by
43	// mutating *Markdown in Run. This keeps the durability model clear: at any
44	// point during Run, the Markdown IS the durable view.
45	type Result struct {
46		// Status: Done | InProgress | Failed | NeedsInput.
47		Status AgentStatus
48	
49		// NextPhase advances the phase frontmatter on Status: Done. Empty
50		// means "stay in current phase" — used for in-place saves between
51		// steps in a multi-step phase.
52		NextPhase string
53	
54		// Message is a human-readable status. Required for Failed/NeedsInput.
55		Message string
56	
57		// ContinueToNext signals whether the StepRunner should proceed to
58		// the next step in the same Job invocation (true) or exit and let
59		// the controller re-trigger the same phase (false).
60		//
61		// Default is exit-after-save. Multi-step phases set this to true on
62		// intermediate steps and let the last step decide.
63		ContinueToNext bool
64	
65		// AgentTurns is the number of conversation turns the session that produced this
66		// result took, from the CLI's own end-of-run summary. Nil means no measurement was
67		// reported — a zero or negative summary is treated as no measurement, and the turn
68		// entry is then omitted from the payload entirely.
69		AgentTurns *int64
70	
71		// InteractionCount is the number of human-authored entries the run's own session
72		// transcript recorded. Nil means the evidence was unavailable — the interaction
73		// entry is omitted from the payload. A non-nil zero is an observation: the
74		// transcript was read and contained no human-authored entry. Absence is never
75		// substituted with a zero.
76		InteractionCount *int64
77	}

14	// Run executes multiple functions concurrently with automatic error logging, panic recovery,
15	// and context.Canceled error filtering. Each function is wrapped with logging, panic recovery,
16	// and error filtering middleware. Returns on first function completion using the
17	// CancelOnFirstFinishWait strategy, which cancels all other functions when any one completes.
18	func Run(ctx context.Context, funcs ...run.Func) error {
19		for i, fn := range funcs {
20			funcs[i] = run.LogErrors(
21				run.CatchPanic(
22					FilterErrors(
23						fn,
24						context.Canceled,
25					),
26				),
27			)
28		}
29		return run.CancelOnFirstFinishWait(ctx, funcs...)
30	}
31	
32	// FilterErrors wraps a run.Func to suppress specified errors, returning nil instead of the error
33	// if it matches any of the provided filteredErrors using errors.Is. This is useful for filtering
34	// out expected errors like context.Canceled during graceful shutdown.
35	func FilterErrors(fn run.Func, filteredErrors ...error) run.Func {
36		return func(ctx context.Context) error {
37			if err := fn(ctx); err != nil {
38				for _, filteredError := range filteredErrors {
39					if errors.Is(err, filteredError) {
40						return nil
41					}
42				}
43				return err
44			}
45			return nil
46		}
47	}

14	// Options configures behavior for service execution, particularly Sentry error reporting.
15	// It allows customization of which errors should be excluded from Sentry reports.
16	type Options struct {
17		ExcludeErrors sentry.ExcludeErrors
18	}
19	
20	// OptionsFn is a functional option pattern function for configuring Options.
21	// It allows callers to customize service behavior by modifying the Options struct.
22	type OptionsFn func(option *Options)
23	
24	// NewOptions creates a new Options instance with sensible defaults and applies the given
25	// functional options. By default, context.Canceled and context.DeadlineExceeded errors
26	// are excluded from Sentry reporting as they represent expected shutdown conditions.
27	// Errors whose chain contains a value implementing interface{ Transient() bool } that
28	// returns true are also excluded, allowing libraries to mark expected, self-resolving
29	// conditions without the framework depending on them.
30	func NewOptions(fns ...OptionsFn) Options {
31		options := Options{
32			ExcludeErrors: sentry.ExcludeErrors{
33				func(err error) bool {
34					return stderrors.Is(err, context.Canceled)
35				},
36				func(err error) bool {
37					return stderrors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)
38				},
39				func(err error) bool {
40					var transient interface{ Transient() bool }
41					return stderrors.As(err, &transient) && transient.Transient()
42				},
43			},
44		}
45		for _, fn := range fns {
46			fn(&options)
47		}
48		return options

include Makefile.variables
include Makefile.precommit
include Makefile.docker

DOCKER_REGISTRY ?= docker.io
IMAGE ?= bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent
ifeq ($(VERSION),)
	VERSION := $(shell git describe --tags `git rev-list --tags --max-count=1`)
endif

# Local dev only. Runtime config (kafka brokers, sentry DSN, stage vars) and the
# full deployment moved to the quant config repo — this is now a publish-only
# source repo (see CHANGELOG). Pass any flags/env locally as needed.
run:
	@go run -mod=mod main.go -v=2

deps:
	go install github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2/ginkgo@v2.25.3
	sudo port install trivy

.PHONY: fix
fix:
	@for dir in $$(find `pwd` -type d -name vendor -prune -o -name go.mod -exec dirname "{}" \; | grep -v '^$$'); do \
		cd $${dir}; \
		echo "fix $${dir}"; \
		go get \
		github.com/bborbe/kv@latest \
		github.com/bborbe/memorykv@latest \
		github.com/bborbe/badgerkv@latest \
		github.com/bborbe/boltkv@latest \
		github.com/go-git/go-git/v5@latest \
		github.com/containerd/containerd@latest \
		golang.org/x/crypto@latest \
		golang.org/x/net@latest; \
	done
=== precommit ===
include tools.env

default: precommit

precommit: ensure format generate shellcheck test check addlicense
	@echo "ready to commit"

# The cluster-build scripts under hack/ handle credentials (teamvault → Secret)
# and run as root inside a Job, so they get a lint pass. `-S warning` keeps it to
# real defects: the SC1091 infos are dynamic `source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/…"` paths
# shellcheck cannot resolve, and they are present in every repo that vendors this
# set. shellcheck ships on GitHub's ubuntu-latest runners, so CI needs no install.
.PHONY: shellcheck
shellcheck:
	shellcheck -S warning hack/*.sh

ensure:
	go mod tidy
	go mod verify
	rm -rf vendor

format:
	find . -type f -name 'go.mod' -not -path './vendor/*' -exec go run github.com/shoenig/go-modtool@$(GO_MODTOOL_VERSION) -w fmt "{}" \;
	go run github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/v3@$(GOIMPORTS_REVISER_VERSION) -project-name github.com/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent -format -excludes vendor ./...
	find . -type d -name vendor -prune -o -type f -name '*.go' -print0 | xargs -0 -n 10 go run github.com/segmentio/golines@$(GOLINES_VERSION) --max-len=100 -w
	find . -type f -name '*.go' -not -path './vendor/*' -exec gofmt -w "{}" +

generate:
	rm -rf mocks avro
	mkdir -p mocks
	echo "package mocks" > mocks/mocks.go
	go generate -mod=mod ./...

.PHONY: generatek8s
generatek8s:
	bash hack/update-codegen.sh

# -race=true catches data races but flakes on some CI runners (rare SIGSEGV
# during gexec.Build in cmd/*-style binary smoke tests). Default off; opt in
# via ENABLE_RACE=true for nightly/manual hardening runs.
TESTFLAGS_RACE = -race=false
ifdef ENABLE_RACE
	TESTFLAGS_RACE = -race=true
endif

.PHONY: test
test:
	go test -mod=mod -p=$${GO_TEST_PARALLEL:-1} -cover $(TESTFLAGS_RACE) $(shell go list -mod=mod ./... | grep -v /vendor/)

check: lint vet vulncheck osv-scanner trivy

lint:
	go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@$(GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION) run --allow-parallel-runners --config .golangci.yml ./...

vet:
	go vet -mod=mod $(shell go list -mod=mod ./... | grep -v /vendor/)

# errcheck is no longer run standalone. `go run github.com/kisielk/errcheck@v1.20.0`
# builds in errcheck's OWN module context, which pins golang.org/x/tools v0.44.0 — a
# reader that stops at export data version 4, while the Go 1.27.2 toolchain emits
# version 5. The target therefore dies with `internal error: package "context" without
# types was imported`, on every repo, at any go.mod directive. It is NOT repairable by
# editing this repo's graph: `ensure` runs `go mod tidy` first, and tidy strips a require
# nothing imports. errcheck is embedded in golangci-lint instead (see .golangci.yml →
# settings.errcheck, which carries the equivalent exclude-functions for the old
# `-ignore '(Close|Write|Fprint)'` flag).

VULNCHECK_IGNORE ?= GO-2026-4923 GO-2026-4514 GO-2022-0470 GO-2026-4772 GO-2026-4771 GO-2026-5932 GO-2026-4970 GO-2026-5856

.PHONY: vulncheck
vulncheck:
	@PKGS="$(shell go list -mod=mod ./... | grep -v /vendor/)"; \
	IGNORE_JSON=$$(printf '%s\n' $(VULNCHECK_IGNORE) | jq -R . | jq -s .); \
	REMAIN=$$(go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@$(GOVULNCHECK_VERSION) -format json $$PKGS 2>/dev/null | \
		jq -rs --argjson ignore "$$IGNORE_JSON" \
			'(map(select(.osv != null)) | map({key: .osv.id, value: (.osv.summary // "")}) | from_entries) as $$sum | \
			 map(select(.finding != null) | .finding) | \
			 map(select(.osv as $$o | $$ignore | index($$o) | not)) | \
			 map("\(.osv)\t\(.trace[-1].module)@\(.trace[-1].version) -> \(.fixed_version)\t\($$sum[.osv] // "")") | \
			 unique | .[]'); \
	if [ -n "$$REMAIN" ]; then \
		echo "Unexpected vulnerabilities (ignored: $(VULNCHECK_IGNORE)):"; \
		printf '%s\n' "$$REMAIN" | column -t -s "$$(printf '\t')"; \
		exit 1; \
	else \
		echo "No unignored vulnerabilities found"; \
	fi

osv-scanner:
	@if [ -f .osv-scanner.toml ]; then \
		echo "Using .osv-scanner.toml"; \
		go run github.com/google/osv-scanner/v2/cmd/osv-scanner@$(OSV_SCANNER_VERSION) --config .osv-scanner.toml --recursive .; \
	else \
		echo "No config found, running default scan"; \
		go run github.com/google/osv-scanner/v2/cmd/osv-scanner@$(OSV_SCANNER_VERSION) --recursive .; \
	fi

# gosec is no longer run standalone, for the same reason as errcheck above: `gosec@$(GOSEC_VERSION)`
# also builds in its own module context and dies at Go 1.27.2 with `internal error: package
# "X" without types was imported`. It is embedded in golangci-lint instead (see .golangci.yml →
# settings.gosec, which carries the equivalent `excludes: [G104]` for the old `-exclude=G104`).

.PHONY: trivy
trivy:
	trivy fs \
	--db-repository ghcr.io/aquasecurity/trivy-db \
	$(if $(wildcard .trivyignore),--ignorefile .trivyignore,$(if $(wildcard $(ROOTDIR)/.trivyignore),--ignorefile $(ROOTDIR)/.trivyignore,)) \
	$(if $(wildcard .trivy-secret.yaml),--secret-config .trivy-secret.yaml,$(if $(wildcard $(ROOTDIR)/.trivy-secret.yaml),--secret-config $(ROOTDIR)/.trivy-secret.yaml,)) \
	--scanners vuln,secret \
	--skip-dirs vendor \
	--quiet \
	--no-progress \
	--disable-telemetry \
	--exit-code 1 .

addlicense:
	go run github.com/google/addlicense@$(ADDLICENSE_VERSION) -c "Benjamin Borbe" -y $$(date +'%Y') -l bsd $$(find . -name "*.go" -not -path './vendor/*')

# fix(delivery): a failed result that advanced no phase publishes no phase

<summary>
- A `Failed` result that advanced no phase no longer republishes the Job-start phase, so a task parked at `human_review` while the Job was running stays parked and no second Job starts
- A `Failed` result whose Job did advance still publishes that advanced phase, so a `planning → execution` run that then fails stays at `execution`
- The `Failed` branch now behaves like the other four non-advancing branches (`Done` without `NextPhase`, `needs_input`, `in_progress`, unknown), which already publish no phase
- When a non-empty Job-start phase is dropped, a verbose log line records it, so the drop is visible in the log rather than only in git history
- Five existing specs that asserted the buggy contract are updated in place (not deleted) to assert the phase key is absent
- A new regression spec reproduces the 2026-10-30 shape using the existing Job-start `planning` fixture
- The four source comments that described the old contract are rewritten so the code and its prose agree
- A changelog entry records the behaviour change
</summary>

<objective>
Make `kafkaResultDeliverer.applyResultFrontmatter`'s `AgentStatusFailed` arm omit the `phase` key when the Job advanced no phase, exactly as the other four non-advancing branches already do, while keeping the advanced-phase publication intact. This stops a failed result from overwriting a phase another writer parked while the Job was still running.
</objective>

<context>
Read `CLAUDE.md` for project conventions and `docs/dod.md` for the repo's definition of done (it requires a `## Unreleased` CHANGELOG entry).

Read these files fully before editing:

- `delivery/result-deliverer.go` (441 lines) — the whole file. The change is in `kafkaResultDeliverer.applyResultFrontmatter`; the four comments to rewrite are in the same file.
- `delivery/result-deliverer_test.go` (1319 lines) — read the Kafka deliverer `Describe` block (starts around line 185) and in particular the `Context("phase advanced in-process within one Job", ...)` starting around line 1079, plus the five `Failed` specs at lines 240-261, 504-525, 527-547, 708-728 and 730-750.
- `docs/task-flow-and-failure-semantics.md` lines 33 and 59 — line 33 states the contract this fix restores: "Controller-side failure paths (`needs_input`, `failed`, cap-exhaustion) leave phase unchanged". Line 59 shows the executor allowlist (`planning`, `in_progress`, `ai_review`), which is why a stale `planning` re-spawns the task while a parked `human_review` does not. Do NOT edit this document — it already describes the correct behaviour.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — the top heading is `## v0.135.0`; there is no `## Unreleased` section today.

Coding guidelines (these live in the YOLO container at the paths shown, not in this repo):

- `/home/node/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/coding/docs/go-glog-guide.md` — the dropped-phase log line is debug-shaped, so it must be gated behind `glog.V(2)`, matching the existing `glog.V(2).Infof` calls in `applyResultMetrics`.
- `/home/node/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/coding/docs/go-testing-guide.md` — Ginkgo v2 / Gomega style, external test package.
- `/home/node/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/coding/docs/changelog-guide.md` — `## Unreleased` entry format and prefix rules.
- `/home/node/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/coding/docs/definition-of-done.md` — changed-behaviour coverage.

## Why the change is safe

The published update is merged downstream by `agent-task-controller`'s `MergeFrontmatter`, which copies the on-disk values first and then overlays the incoming ones. A key absent from the payload therefore keeps its on-disk value. This is the same mechanism the four non-advancing branches already rely on (`delete(frontmatter, "phase")` appears in the `Done`-without-`NextPhase`, `needs_input`, `in_progress` and `default` arms of the same function). The `Failed` arm is the only one that does not, and it is the arm that fires on the most common non-advancing outcome: a pod crash before any phase write.

## Cross-repo ordering constraint (do not implement here)

The controller's planning-retry gate (`bborbe/agent-task-controller`, `pkg/command/planning_retry.go`, `matchesRetryGate`) currently reads the phase from the published payload. Once this deliverer stops sending a phase on a non-advancing failure, that gate would skip. The controller-side change — read the on-disk phase instead — is a **separate spec and PR** and is explicitly out of scope here. Do not add it, do not vendor a workaround, and do not change `MergeFrontmatter` (it lives in the controller repo). The controller change must land and deploy before or with this one; mention that ordering in the changelog entry.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## v0.6.2

- fix: link the pinned dark-factory clone to `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/dark-factory` so the authoring-rule paths the agents hardcode resolve — a local-path `marketplace add` never creates that directory, so prompt generation ran with no guides

## v0.6.1

- chore: restate the `do-not-merge` gate message to name its bypass actors — the Admin repository role and Integration `3907226`, both `bypass_mode: always` in the `master-protection` ruleset — instead of asserting an unqualified block

## v0.6.0

- feat: **build the release image on a cluster (`BUILD_TARGET=sun`), not only locally.** `make build` had a single arm — a local `docker build` — so publishing a release required a Docker daemon and `docker push` on the workstation. An agent is refused `docker push`, which made a release image unpublishable without a human at the keyboard. `Makefile.docker` now carries two arms, ported from `bborbe/a2a-worker-controller` and `bborbe/agent-claude`: `BUILD_TARGET=local` (the default, unchanged behaviour) and any other value, which renders `hack/build-job.yaml` as a Job on that cluster and pushes from inside it. The vendored `hack/` set is `a2a-worker-controller`'s hardened copy — templated namespace, `case`-based value whitelisting, no service-account token — rather than `agent-claude`'s older one. The cluster arm refuses to run without an explicit `VERSION` (the Makefile default is the newest release tag, so a defaulted build would overwrite a published image with one built from a different commit) and refuses to push a `vX.Y.Z` tag from any `REF` other than that tag. `upload` and `clean` are guarded so a remote build does not fail at a push step for an image that was never local. `Dockerfile` gains a `go mod vendor` step in its build stage: the local arm got `vendor/` from `check-go-mod`, but the cluster arm clones a git ref where `vendor/` is gitignored, so `-mod=vendor` would have failed there. `make precommit` now runs `shellcheck -S warning` over `hack/*.sh`, since those scripts handle the teamvault→Secret credential path

## v0.5.14

- fix: **redact the `AnthropicAuthToken` value from the startup argument dump.** The root binary's `application` struct carried `display:"password"` — a tag the argument printer does not implement. It honours only `display:"hidden"` and `display:"length"`, so every other value fell through to the plaintext branch (`Argument: %s '%v'`) and each Job start wrote the live model-router credential in cleartext into the cluster Job log. The field now carries `display:"length"`, matching the sibling in `cmd/run-task`, so the dump names the key and its length and never the value. A regression spec drives the real printer over the real struct and fails if the redaction is removed

## v0.5.13

- test: **cover the per-prompt setup fetch, not only the push.** `v0.5.12` moved the credential to a file-backed git helper, but only the push site had a regression spec — the fetch site (the one that failed first on 2026-11-03) was pinned by nothing. The new spec starts with token `A`, lets the lifecycle refresher mint `B`, and asserts the credential `git credential fill` resolves *during* the run is `B` — the A→B shape a "file is non-empty" check would not discriminate. No production code changes

## v0.5.12

- fix: **install a file-backed git credential helper so a long lifecycle run never uses an expired token.** The GitHub App installation token lives 60 minutes and is minted once at startup; `gh auth setup-git` binds it into a helper that resolves `GH_TOKEN` from the environment of whatever runs git, and the dark-factory daemon captured that environment when it was started — so no refresh in the parent process can reach it. A token file has no such lifetime: git re-reads it at every credential lookup. Observed 2026-11-03 on `bborbe/trading#433`: token minted 18:10Z, the daemon's own `git fetch origin` refused at 19:15Z with `Invalid username or token. Password authentication is not supported`

## v0.5.11

- fix: **exit non-zero when the agent publishes `Status: failed`.** The result was still published to the task, but the process returned nil, so the Job completed and the executor — which records a phase success on exit 0 alone (`IsJobSucceeded` in `agent-task-executor`'s `job_watcher`) and never reads the published Status — wrote a *phase success* for a run that had failed. Once the success grace expired the task was parked at `human_review` as though a human had parked it deliberately. Observed 2026-11-03 on task `ceb79961`: a Job that published `Status: failed` for `git clone --bare: Failed to connect to github.com port 443` exited 0 and parked the task. `needs_input` is deliberately unchanged — parking for a human answer is that status's intent

## v0.5.10

- chore: update github.com/bborbe/agent to v0.138.0, github.com/bborbe/cqrs to v0.6.15, github.com/bborbe/errors to v1.6.6, github.com/bborbe/kafka to v1.29.11, github.com/bborbe/maintainer to v0.51.0, github.com/bborbe/sentry to v1.10.7, github.com/bborbe/service to v1.11.2, github.com/bborbe/time to v1.27.25, github.com/bborbe/vault-cli to v0.186.2, github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2 to v2.34.0

# github-dark-factory-agent — design.md

Design artifact for the Phase-2 gate of [[Lift Dark-Factory Daemon into Agent Framework]]. Produced via `/agent:launch-agent` (which walks the [[Agent Design Guide]] interview) on 2026-07-12, drawing on the Phase-1 prototype E2E (both slash-command prototypes validated on `bborbe/go-skeleton` PR #37 through merge).

## Part 1 — Motivation

- **Problem:** dark-factory's spec→prompt→execute lifecycle runs locally (`/dark-factory:daemon` / `run`), tying autonomous coding to one author + one awake laptop.
- **Do-nothing cost:** throughput capped at one author × one machine; no laptop-free execution.
- **This agent:** the cluster implementer. A human drafts + approves a spec on a draft-PR branch and walks away; this agent implements it and lands the task at `human_review`; the human verifies + flips the PR to ready; the existing `github-pr-review-agent` reviews + merges. Two human bookends, autonomous middle.

## Part 2 — Identity

- **Name / repo:** `github-dark-factory-agent` → `github.com/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent` (matches `github-pr-review-agent`, `github-releaser-agent` post-split convention). Image `docker.io/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent`.
- **Assignee (Config CRD `spec.assignee`):** `github-dark-factory-agent` — MUST match the `assignee` the watcher emits.
- **Pattern:** B (k8s Job per task). **Shape:** claude (mirrors `github-pr-review-agent`).
- **Runtime:** the Job pod IS a claude-yolo container (claude + git + gh + dark-factory CLI baked in).

## Part 3 — Integration

- **Trigger:** `github-dark-factory-watcher` (Phase-1: `/github-dark-factory-watcher` slash command; Phase-3: Go watcher). Emits when a draft PR has `.dark-factory.yaml` + ≥1 `approved`-not-`completed` spec **that appears in the PR's own diff** (diff-scoping — validated fix; "spec exists on branch" alone false-triggers on repos that persist specs).
- **Task contract:** [[Agent Task File Contract]] — `task_type: dark-factory-implement`, `assignee: github-dark-factory-agent`, `repo`/`clone_url`/`ref`/`pr_number`/`branch`; body is an operator-readable header, the clone is the data source.
- **Downstream:** lands task at `phase: human_review` (never flips the PR). Human flips draft→ready → `github-pr-watcher` → `github-pr-review-agent`.

## Part 4 — Behavior (phases)

| Phase | Impl shape | Reads | Side effects | Writes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| planning | pure-Go spec scan (`agent/code` shape) | frontmatter (`clone_url`,`ref`,`branch`,`pr_number`) | clone branch, precondition checks (ref==HEAD, `.dark-factory.yaml`, approved-not-completed spec, PR draft) | `## Plan` |
| execution | custom step (dark-factory lifecycle + git) | `## Plan` | generate prompts → audit+approve → execute → verify → `spec complete`; commit + push per prompt | `## Result` |
| ai_review | `claudelib.NewAgentStep` (read-only) | `## Plan`+`## Result` | remote checks: all specs `completed`, no prompts in-flight, PR still draft, diff-vs-spec sanity | `## Review`; `phase: human_review`, clear assignee |

**Never runs `gh pr ready`.** The human's flip is the verification sign-off.

## Part 4.2 — ✅ Execution engine dependency (RESOLVED — shipped + live-validated)

The Phase-1 E2E surfaced a hard requirement: **dark-factory spawned nested claude-yolo containers** for the LLM steps. Since this agent's Job pod is *already* a claude-yolo container, that is DinD — disallowed (goal Non-goal).

**Prerequisite SHIPPED (2026-07-13): dark-factory `backend: local`** — a second `pkg/executor.Executor` (`localSubprocessExecutor`) that runs `claude` directly in the current process/cwd instead of `docker run`. Selected via config or `dark-factory run --set backend=local`. Git orchestration stays in the binary unchanged. Landed as spec 104, released **v0.192.0** (docs v0.192.1, scenario 024 v0.192.2). The agent's Dockerfile pins `DARK_FACTORY_VERSION=v0.192.0`.

**Live-validated 2026-07-13** with a real `dark-factory run --set`-style config (`backend: local`, `workflow: direct`, bare-remote sandbox):
- **Happy path:** a real approved prompt → claude ran **in-process (~11s), zero docker containers** → produced the change → `git commit` → prompt `completed`. This is the exact loop the execution step drives.
- **Fail path:** claude absent → fails closed (`claude not found on PATH`), no docker (scenario 024, `active`).

So the agent invokes `dark-factory run` (or per-prompt equivalents) with `--set backend=local` and lets dark-factory's Go binary do git; no nested containers, no DinD.

## Part 5 — Data contract & invariants

- Config via `--set` at runtime, NEVER committed to the PR branch (committed `.dark-factory.yaml` divergence conflicts `workflow:direct`'s `git merge origin/master`). Keep the branch current with `origin/<default>`.
- **★ claude auth is HOME-sensitive (live-smoke finding 2026-07-13).** `backend: local` runs `claude` as a subprocess inheriting the pod's env. If `claude`'s login credential is not discoverable from the process's `HOME`, every prompt fails fast with `Not logged in · Please run /login` (observed: overriding `HOME` broke auth even with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set). **Requirement:** the Job pod MUST provision claude's login where the agent process's `HOME` resolves it — bake/mount the credential into the runtime `HOME` (claude-yolo image convention), do NOT rely on `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` alone. Add a startup precondition check: run a trivial `claude --print` (or reuse dark-factory's claude probe) and fail the task early with a clear escalation if unauthed, rather than failing every prompt.
- **★ the dark-factory Claude PLUGIN must be installed, not just the CLI (E2E root cause 2026-07-13).** backend:local's generation and prompt-audit steps run the slash commands `/dark-factory:generate-prompts-for-spec` and `/dark-factory:audit-prompt` *inside* claude. If the runtime `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` has the CLI binary but not the plugin, claude reports `Unknown command: /dark-factory:generate-prompts-for-spec` → **zero prompts generated → the spec resets to `approved` and the daemon idles at "nothing to do"** (silent — no error surfaces to the agent; looks like a generation-trigger bug but is really a provisioning gap). **Requirement:** the Dockerfile installs the plugin at build time (`claude plugin marketplace add bborbe/dark-factory && claude plugin install dark-factory@dark-factory`, verified with `claude plugin list | grep -q dark-factory`), mirroring github-pr-review-agent's build-time `coding` install. Keep the plugin's minor aligned with `DARK_FACTORY_VERSION`.
- **★ backend:local ignores dark-factory `config.env` (spec-104 gap).** `pkg/executor.localSubprocessExecutor.buildCommand` passes `--model` from config but never sets `cmd.Env` — so the subprocess inherits only the *ambient* process env. Unlike the docker backend (which injects `config.env` into the container), backend:local does NOT apply `env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` / token from `~/.config/dark-factory/config.yaml`. **Requirement:** the Job pod sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (model router) and the auth token as **pod env vars**, not via dark-factory `config.env`. (Follow-up: dark-factory could merge `config.env` into the local subprocess env so one config works for both backends.)
- Agent MUST drive `dark-factory spec complete` (else spec stays `verifying` = approved-not-completed → watcher re-emits).
- Idempotency: `AgentStep.ShouldRun` checks if the phase's `##` section exists; per-prompt commits make execution crash-resumable.
- Concurrency: per-repo cap 1 (Config CRD) — two PRs on one repo must not race git push.

## Part 6 — Operations

- Pattern B Job (not cron); resource profile ~ `github-pr-review-agent`.
- Kill switch: remove/disable the Config CRD.
- Observability: phase-transition logs + metrics; per-prompt execution visible.

# Agent Guardrails

Headless task execution agent running in a container.

## Scope

- Execute ONLY the task in the `## Task` section
- Do NOT take actions beyond task scope
- Do NOT explore or enumerate systems beyond what the task requires

## Forbidden

- **No internal network access** — never access internal domains, K8s metadata (169.254.169.254), cluster DNS (*.svc, *.local), or private IPs (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x). Public internet is allowed for documentation and research.
- **No package installation** — no apt/apk/npm/pip/go install

5	// Command github-dark-factory-agent is the canonical AI-heavy agent: one Claude
6	// invocation per phase, all logic in the prompt + allowed tools.
7	//
8	// This binary is the Kafka entry point — spawned as a K8s Job by
9	// task/executor with TASK_CONTENT + TASK_ID + PHASE + KAFKA_BROKERS env.
10	// For local CLI mode (file-based), see cmd/run-task/main.go.
11	//
12	// Reference implementation for AI-heavy agents using the agent framework
13	// (lib.NewAgent + claude.NewAgentStep). Other agents (trade-analysis,
14	// pr-reviewer) follow the same shape — copy this main.go and swap
15	// prompts/tools.
16	package main
17	
18	import (
19		"context"
20		"os"
21		"time"
22	
23		agentlib "github.com/bborbe/agent"
24		claudelib "github.com/bborbe/agent/claude"
25		delivery "github.com/bborbe/agent/delivery"
26		"github.com/bborbe/agent/envparse"
27		libmetrics "github.com/bborbe/agent/metrics"
28		"github.com/bborbe/cqrs/base"
29		"github.com/bborbe/errors"
30		libkafka "github.com/bborbe/kafka"
31		githubapp "github.com/bborbe/maintainer/githubapp"
32		libsentry "github.com/bborbe/sentry"
33		"github.com/bborbe/service"
34		libtime "github.com/bborbe/time"
35		"github.com/bborbe/vault-cli/pkg/domain"
36		"github.com/golang/glog"
37		"github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus"
38		"github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/push"
39	
40		"github.com/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent/pkg/factory"
41		"github.com/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent/pkg/githubauth"
42	)
43	
44	// agentName is the identity string used for Prometheus metric grouping and logging.
45	const agentName = "github-dark-factory-agent"
46	
47	func main() {
48		app := &application{}
49		os.Exit(service.Main(context.Background(), app, &app.SentryDSN, &app.SentryProxy))
50	}
51	
52	type application struct {
53		SentryDSN   string `required:"false" arg:"sentry-dsn"   env:"SENTRY_DSN"   usage:"SentryDSN"    display:"length"`
54		SentryProxy string `required:"false" arg:"sentry-proxy" env:"SENTRY_PROXY" usage:"Sentry Proxy" display:"length"`
55	
56		// Claude Code CLI configuration
57		ClaudeConfigDir claudelib.ClaudeConfigDir `required:"false" arg:"claude-config-dir" env:"CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR" usage:"Claude Code config directory"`
58	
59		// Agent directory (contains .claude/ with CLAUDE.md and commands)
60		AgentDir claudelib.AgentDir `required:"false" arg:"agent-dir" env:"AGENT_DIR" usage:"Agent directory with .claude/ config" default:"agent"`
61	
62		// Allowed tools (comma-separated)
63		AllowedToolsRaw string `required:"false" arg:"allowed-tools" env:"ALLOWED_TOOLS" usage:"Comma-separated list of allowed tools"`
64	
65		// Task content from agent pipeline
66		TaskContent string `required:"true" arg:"task-content" env:"TASK_CONTENT" usage:"Raw task markdown from vault"`
67	
68		// Environment context passed to prompt (comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs)
69		EnvContextRaw string `required:"false" arg:"env-context" env:"ENV_CONTEXT" usage:"Comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs for prompt context"`
70	
71		// Environment variables passed to Claude CLI process (comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs).
72		// Use this for ad-hoc / less-common env vars. The three load-bearing Anthropic provider
73		// vars below have dedicated arg slots so they don't have to be packed into this string.
74		ClaudeEnvRaw string `required:"false" arg:"claude-env" env:"CLAUDE_ENV" usage:"Comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs for Claude CLI environment"`
75	
76		// Anthropic-compatible provider routing. Setting AnthropicBaseURL + AnthropicAuthToken
77		// routes the claude CLI to an alt-provider (e.g. MiniMax via https://api.minimax.io/anthropic).
78		// AnthropicModel drives both the `--model` CLI flag and the ANTHROPIC_MODEL env var seen by
79		// the claude subprocess. Non-empty values override the same keys in ClaudeEnvRaw.
80		AnthropicBaseURL   string                `required:"false" arg:"anthropic-base-url"   env:"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"   usage:"Anthropic-compatible API base URL"`
81		AnthropicAuthToken string                `required:"false" arg:"anthropic-auth-token" env:"ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN" usage:"Bearer token for ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"                                  display:"length"`
82		AnthropicModel     claudelib.ClaudeModel `required:"false" arg:"anthropic-model"      env:"ANTHROPIC_MODEL"      usage:"Model name; also exposed to the claude subprocess as ANTHROPIC_MODEL"                  default:"sonnet"`
83	
84		// Branch for Kafka result delivery
85		Branch base.Branch `required:"false" arg:"branch" env:"BRANCH" usage:"branch"`
86	
87		// TopicPrefix is an explicit Kafka topic prefix, independent of Branch.
88		TopicPrefix base.TopicPrefix `required:"false" arg:"topic-prefix" env:"TOPIC_PREFIX" usage:"Explicit Kafka topic prefix; empty means unprefixed topics"`
89	
90		// Phase to run (framework requires explicit phase)
91		Phase domain.TaskPhase `required:"false" arg:"phase" env:"PHASE" usage:"Agent phase: planning | execution | ai_review" default:"execution"`
92	
93		// GitHub token for authenticated clones + REST API calls (planning phase).
94		// Used as the raw fallback credential when GitHub App creds are absent
95		// (local cmd/run-task path where the operator exports `gh auth token`).
96		GhToken string `required:"false" arg:"gh-token" env:"GH_TOKEN" usage:"GitHub token for clone + PR inspection (raw fallback when App creds unset)" display:"length"`
97	
98		// GitHub App authentication. When APP_ID, INSTALLATION_ID, and a PEM (file
99		// or inline) are all set, the pod mints a short-lived installation access
100		// token at startup and forwards it to every git/gh subprocess as GH_TOKEN.
101		// The cluster pod sets these (GH_TOKEN is empty there); locally they are
102		// absent and the agent falls back to the raw GhToken above.
103		AppID          int64  `required:"false" arg:"app-id"          env:"APP_ID"          usage:"GitHub App ID (numeric); enables App auth when set with INSTALLATION_ID + PEM"`
104		InstallationID int64  `required:"false" arg:"installation-id" env:"INSTALLATION_ID" usage:"GitHub App Installation ID (numeric)"`
105		PEMKeyFile     string `required:"false" arg:"pem-key-file"    env:"PEM_KEY_FILE"    usage:"Path to the GitHub App private key (PEM file mounted from k8s Secret)"`
106		PEMKey         string `required:"false" arg:"pem-key"         env:"PEM_KEY"         usage:"GitHub App private key (PEM) as env var content; mutually exclusive with PEM_KEY_FILE" display:"length"`
107	
108		// Workdir paths for bare-clone cache and per-task worktrees.
109		ReposPath string `required:"false" arg:"repos-path" env:"REPOS_PATH" usage:"Root path for bare-clone cache"   default:"/repos"`
110		WorkPath  string `required:"false" arg:"work-path"  env:"WORK_PATH"  usage:"Root path for per-task worktrees" default:"/work"`
111	
112		// Kafka delivery (optional — only active when TASK_ID is set)
113		KafkaBrokers libkafka.Brokers        `required:"false" arg:"kafka-brokers" env:"KAFKA_BROKERS" usage:"Comma separated list of Kafka brokers"`
114		TaskID       agentlib.TaskIdentifier `required:"false" arg:"task-id"       env:"TASK_ID"       usage:"Agent task identifier for publishing results back to task controller"`
115	
116		PushgatewayURL string `required:"false" arg:"pushgateway-url" env:"PUSHGATEWAY_URL" usage:"Prometheus PushGateway URL"          default:"http://pushgateway:9090"`
117		TaskType       string `required:"false" arg:"task-type"       env:"TASK_TYPE"       usage:"Task type label for metric grouping" default:"unknown"`
118	}
119	
120	func (a *application) Run(ctx context.Context, _ libsentry.Client) error {
121		registry := prometheus.NewRegistry()
122		jobMetrics := libmetrics.NewJobMetrics(registry, libtime.NewCurrentDateTime())
123		pusher := push.New(a.PushgatewayURL, libmetrics.BuildJobMetricsName(agentName)).
124			Grouping("agent", agentName).
125			Grouping("task_type", a.TaskType).
126			Collector(registry)
127		defer func() {
128			if err := pusher.PushContext(ctx); err != nil {
129				glog.Warningf("prometheus push failed: %v", err)
130				return
131			}
132			glog.V(2).Infof("prometheus push completed")
133		}()
134		start := libtime.NewCurrentDateTime().Now().Time()
135	
136		glog.V(2).Infof("github-dark-factory-agent started phase=%s", a.Phase)
137	
138		// Resolve the GitHub credential (App IAT or raw GH_TOKEN fallback) and make
139		// it usable by every git/gh subprocess. See prepareAuth.
140		resolvedToken, err := a.prepareAuth(ctx)
141		if err != nil {
142			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
143			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
144			return err
145		}
146	
147		deliverer := delivery.NewNoopResultDeliverer()
148		if a.TaskID != "" {
149			if len(a.KafkaBrokers) == 0 {
150				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
151				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
152				return errors.Errorf(ctx, "KAFKA_BROKERS must be set when TASK_ID is set")
153			}
154			syncProducer, err := factory.CreateSyncProducer(ctx, a.KafkaBrokers)
155			if err != nil {
156				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
157				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
158				return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "create sync producer")
159			}
160			defer func() {
161				if err := syncProducer.Close(); err != nil {
162					glog.Warningf("close sync producer failed: %v", err)
163				}
164			}()
165			deliverer = factory.CreateKafkaResultDeliverer(
166				syncProducer, a.TopicPrefix, a.TaskID, a.TaskContent,
167				libtime.NewCurrentDateTime(),
168			)
169		}
170	
171		claudeEnv := a.buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken)
172	
173		repoManager := factory.CreateRepoManager(a.ReposPath, a.WorkPath, resolvedToken)
174		githubClient := factory.CreateGitHubClient(resolvedToken)
175		claudeProber := factory.CreateClaudeProber(a.ClaudeConfigDir)
176		provider := factory.CreateAgentProvider(
177			a.ClaudeConfigDir,
178			a.AgentDir,
179			a.AnthropicModel,
180			resolvedToken,
181			claudeEnv,
182			repoManager,
183			githubClient,
184			claudeProber,
185			// Re-mint before the push: the installation token is minted once here at
186			// startup and expires after 60 minutes, but a lifecycle run routinely
187			// takes longer, so the final push would be refused as an invalid token.
188			a.resolveAuth,
189		)
190		agent, err := provider.Get(ctx, agentlib.TaskType(a.TaskType))
191		if err != nil {
192			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
193			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
194			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "select agent for task_type")
195		}
196	
197		result, err := agent.Run(ctx, a.Phase, a.TaskContent, deliverer)
198		if err != nil {
199			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
200			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
201			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "agent run failed")
202		}
203		jobMetrics.RecordRun(result.Status)
204		jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
205		return finishRun(ctx, result, a.Phase)
206	}
207	
208	// finishRun publishes the agent's result and then decides the Job's exit code.
209	// It exists as one call so Run stays within its funlen budget.
210	func finishRun(
211		ctx context.Context,
212		result *agentlib.Result,
213		phase domain.TaskPhase,
214	) error {
215		if err := agentlib.PrintResult(ctx, result); err != nil {
216			return err
217		}
218		return exitErrorForStatus(ctx, result.Status, phase)
219	}
220	
221	// exitErrorForStatus returns a non-nil error when the agent's published status
222	// must fail the Job, and nil when the Job may exit 0.
223	//
224	// A failed result is still published to the task, but the Job must also exit
225	// non-zero. The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded
226	// in agent-task-executor's job_watcher), so returning nil here makes a failed run
227	// indistinguishable from a completed one: the failure is written as a phase
228	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at human_review
229	// as though a human had parked it deliberately (2026-11-03, task ceb79961: a Job
230	// that published Status=failed for a git clone error exited 0 and parked the
231	// task).
232	//
233	// needs_input is deliberately NOT a failure: parking for a human answer is that
234	// status's intent, and it reaches the same park path on purpose.
235	func exitErrorForStatus(
236		ctx context.Context,
237		status agentlib.AgentStatus,
238		phase domain.TaskPhase,
239	) error {
240		if status == agentlib.AgentStatusFailed {
241			return errors.Errorf(
242				ctx,
243				"agent reported status %q for phase %q",
244				status,
245				phase,
246			)
247		}
248		return nil
249	}

251	// buildClaudeEnv assembles the Claude CLI subprocess env from the raw env
252	// pairs plus the Anthropic provider-routing overrides. resolvedToken, when
253	// non-empty, is threaded in as GH_TOKEN — the ai_review phase's Claude
254	// subprocess shells `gh pr view/diff`, and the runner strips pod env to an
255	// allowlist, so the token must be passed explicitly (os.Setenv in prepareAuth
256	// covers the dark-factory daemon path, not the Claude runner).
257	func (a *application) buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken string) map[string]string {
258		claudeEnv := envparse.KeyValuePairs(a.ClaudeEnvRaw)
259		if claudeEnv == nil {
260			claudeEnv = map[string]string{}
261		}
262		if a.AnthropicBaseURL != "" {
263			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"] = a.AnthropicBaseURL
264		}
265		if a.AnthropicAuthToken != "" {
266			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"] = a.AnthropicAuthToken
267		}
268		if a.AnthropicModel != "" {
269			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_MODEL"] = a.AnthropicModel.String()
270		}
271		if resolvedToken != "" {
272			claudeEnv["GH_TOKEN"] = resolvedToken
273		}
274		return claudeEnv
275	}
276	
277	// prepareAuth resolves the GitHub credential and makes it usable by every
278	// git/gh subprocess: it exports GH_TOKEN (covering the dark-factory daemon,
279	// which inherits os.Environ() for its `git push`) and installs git's credential
280	// helper via `gh auth setup-git`. Returns the resolved token for the
281	// RepoManager / GitHub client / gh-token preflight wiring.
282	func (a *application) prepareAuth(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
283		resolvedToken, err := a.resolveAuth(ctx)
284		if err != nil {
285			return "", err
286		}
287		// resolvedToken is always non-empty here (resolveAuth errors otherwise), but
288		// guard defensively — an empty GH_TOKEN would mislead the daemon subprocess.
289		if resolvedToken != "" {
290			if err := os.Setenv("GH_TOKEN", resolvedToken); err != nil {
291				return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "export GH_TOKEN")
292			}
293		}
294		if err := githubauth.NewGhAuthSetupGit(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
295			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "gh auth setup-git")
296		}
297		// A file the daemon re-reads outlives the token bound into gh's helper: the
298		// installation token expires after 60 minutes and the lifecycle daemon keeps
299		// its startup environment, so a long run's own `git fetch` would use a dead
300		// token (2026-11-03, bborbe/trading#433).
301		if err := githubauth.NewFileBackedHelper(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
302			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "configure file-backed credential helper")
303		}
304		return resolvedToken, nil
305	}
306	
307	// resolveAuth resolves the GitHub credential forwarded to every git/gh
308	// subprocess. It prefers GitHub App authentication: when APP_ID,
309	// INSTALLATION_ID, and a PEM (file or inline) are all set, it mints a
310	// short-lived installation access token via githubapp.MintIAT. Otherwise it
311	// falls back to the raw GH_TOKEN input — the local cmd/run-task path where the
312	// operator exports `gh auth token`. When neither is configured it returns a
313	// clear error, since the agent cannot clone or push without a credential.
314	//
315	// The token is a runtime value (not a config input), so it is returned to the
316	// caller rather than stored on the argument-parsed application struct —
317	// argument/v2 panics when reflecting over unexported struct fields at startup.
318	func (a *application) resolveAuth(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
319		hasPEMFile := a.PEMKeyFile != ""
320		hasPEMContent := a.PEMKey != ""
321		useGitHubApp := a.AppID != 0 && a.InstallationID != 0 && (hasPEMFile || hasPEMContent)
322		if useGitHubApp {
323			appCfg := githubapp.Config{AppID: a.AppID, InstallationID: a.InstallationID}
324			if hasPEMFile {
325				appCfg.PEMPath = a.PEMKeyFile
326			} else {
327				appCfg.PEM = []byte(a.PEMKey)
328			}
329			// Startup auth must not be killed by the task's work deadline: mint on a
330			// fresh bounded context (keeps ctx values, drops the caller's
331			// deadline/cancel) so a near-deadline task can't fail the token mint.
332			mintCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 30*time.Second)
333			defer cancel()
334			iat, err := githubapp.MintIAT(mintCtx, appCfg)
335			if err != nil {
336				return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "mint github app iat")
337			}
338			glog.V(2).Infof(
339				"github-dark-factory-agent auth mode=github-app app_id=%d installation_id=%d",
340				a.AppID, a.InstallationID,
341			)
342			return iat, nil
343		}
344		if a.GhToken != "" {
345			glog.V(2).Infof("github-dark-factory-agent auth mode=gh-token (raw GH_TOKEN fallback)")
346			return a.GhToken, nil
347		}
348		return "", errors.Errorf(
349			ctx,
350			"github-dark-factory-agent auth: no credentials configured — set GitHub App creds (APP_ID, INSTALLATION_ID, PEM_KEY_FILE or PEM_KEY) or GH_TOKEN",
351		)
352	}

20	// TestExitErrorForStatus guards the exit-code contract between this agent and
21	// the executor that watches its Job.
22	//
23	// The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded in
24	// agent-task-executor's job_watcher) and never reads the Status this agent
25	// publishes. So a run that reports failure but exits 0 is written as a phase
26	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at
27	// human_review as though a human had parked it deliberately.
28	//
29	// Observed 2026-11-03: task ceb79961 published Status=failed for
30	// "git clone --bare: Failed to connect to github.com port 443", exited 0, and
31	// parked at human_review.
32	func TestExitErrorForStatus(t *testing.T) {
33		ctx := context.Background()
34		phase := domain.TaskPhase("execution")
35	
36		cases := []struct {
37			name    string
38			status  agentlib.AgentStatus
39			wantErr bool
40		}{
41			{
42				name:    "failed must fail the Job so the executor does not record a phase success",
43				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusFailed,
44				wantErr: true,
45			},
46			{
47				name:    "done exits 0",
48				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusDone,
49				wantErr: false,
50			},
51			{
52				name:    "in_progress exits 0",
53				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusInProgress,
54				wantErr: false,
55			},
56			{
57				// needs_input reaches the same park path on purpose: the task is meant
58				// to wait at human_review for an answer, not to be re-driven.
59				name:    "needs_input exits 0 — parking for a human answer is its intent",
60				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusNeedsInput,
61				wantErr: false,
62			},
63		}
64	
65		for _, c := range cases {
66			t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
67				err := exitErrorForStatus(ctx, c.status, phase)
68				if c.wantErr && err == nil {
69					t.Fatalf(
70						"status %q: expected a non-nil error, got nil — the Job would exit 0 and the executor would record it as a phase success",
71						c.status,
72					)
73				}
74				if !c.wantErr && err != nil {
75					t.Fatalf("status %q: expected nil, got %v", c.status, err)
76				}
77			})
78		}
79	}
80	
81	// TestPrintRedactsAnthropicAuthToken guards the startup argument dump against
82	// republishing the ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN value into the Job log.
83	//
84	// argument.Print honours only display:"hidden" and display:"length"; every other
85	// tag value falls through to the plaintext branch (`Argument: %s '%v'`). The root
86	// binary's application struct carried display:"password" — a value the printer does
87	// not implement — so each Job start wrote the live model-router credential in
88	// cleartext. This test drives the real printer over the real struct, so removing
89	// the display:"length" tag turns it red.
90	//
91	// Plain testing rather than Ginkgo on purpose: application is unexported, so the
92	// assertion must live in package main, and package main_test (main_test.go) shares
93	// this test binary — where a second RunSpecs fails with "calling RunSpecs more than
94	// once". An internal spec therefore cannot join the existing suite. Same shape as
95	// TestExitErrorForStatus above.
96	func TestPrintRedactsAnthropicAuthToken(t *testing.T) {
97		const sentinel = "sentinel-token-do-not-log-9f3a2b7c1d"
98	
99		var buf bytes.Buffer
100		log.SetOutput(&buf)
101		log.SetFlags(0)
102		defer func() {
103			log.SetOutput(os.Stderr)
104			log.SetFlags(log.LstdFlags)
105		}()
106	
107		if err := argument.Print(context.Background(), &application{AnthropicAuthToken: sentinel}); err != nil {
108			t.Fatalf("print: %v", err)
109		}
110	
111		rendered := buf.String()
112		if got := strings.Count(rendered, sentinel); got != 0 {
113			t.Fatalf(
114				"token value leaked into the argument dump: sentinel appeared %d times\n%s",
115				got,
116				rendered,
117			)
118		}
119		if got := strings.Count(rendered, "AnthropicAuthToken"); got != 1 {
120			t.Fatalf("want the field named exactly once, got %d\n%s", got, rendered)
121		}
122		if !strings.Contains(rendered, "Argument: AnthropicAuthToken length ") {
123			t.Fatalf("want the length form, got:\n%s", rendered)
124		}
125	}

# Definition of Done

The validation prompt dark-factory runs against each executed prompt before it
marks the prompt complete. A change is Done only when every box holds.

- [ ] Builds: `make precommit` exits 0 (generate + format + test + lint + vet + gosec + coverage).
- [ ] Tests: new/changed behavior has Ginkgo coverage; boundaries are mocked (counterfeiter), the framework Agent is not.
- [ ] Scope: the diff touches only what the spec asked for; no unrelated files.
- [ ] Errors: wrapped via `github.com/bborbe/errors`; no bare `return err`, no `fmt.Errorf`.
- [ ] Escalation doctrine: failure paths return `Status: failed`/`needs_input` without mutating `assignee`/`status` or writing a `## Failure` section.
- [ ] Docs: user-facing behavior changes are reflected in `docs/` and the CHANGELOG `## Unreleased` section.

=== definition-of-done guide ===
# Definition of Done — Dark Factory Prompts

Rules that every dark-factory prompt execution must satisfy before reporting success.

## Test Coverage

**New code** (new files, new packages):
- Aim for ≥80% statement coverage
- Test all public functions
- Test error paths and edge cases (empty input, nil, invalid values)

**Modified code** (changes to existing files):
- Test all changed/added code paths — every new branch, every new condition
- Existing untested code does NOT need retroactive coverage
- If adding a new field/method to a struct, test the new behavior

**Verification (Go):**
```bash
go test -coverprofile=/tmp/cover.out -mod=vendor ./affected/pkg/...
go tool cover -func=/tmp/cover.out | grep "changed_file"
```

**Verification (Python):**
```bash
pytest --cov=affected_module --cov-report=term-missing
```

## Code Quality

- Follow project CLAUDE.md conventions
- Follow all relevant docs in `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/coding/docs/`
- This includes ALL guides (Go, Python, shell, documentation, etc.) — not just language-specific ones
- Self-review diff against the checklist in CLAUDE.md before `make precommit`

## Verification

- `make test` after each meaningful change (fast feedback)
- `make precommit` once at the end (full validation)
- **Multi-service repos:** only run in the changed service directory, never at repo root
- **YAML/config-only changes:** skip `make precommit`, use the prompt's `<verification>` commands
- Non-zero exit code from `make precommit` = failed, no exceptions

## Changelog

- Update `CHANGELOG.md` with `## Unreleased` entry if project has one
- See `changelog-guide.md` for format rules

## Completion

- Report honest status: success only if `make precommit` exit code 0
- Include verification command and exit code in report

=== docs/design.md Part 4/5 ===
- **Trigger:** `github-dark-factory-watcher` (Phase-1: `/github-dark-factory-watcher` slash command; Phase-3: Go watcher). Emits when a draft PR has `.dark-factory.yaml` + ≥1 `approved`-not-`completed` spec **that appears in the PR's own diff** (diff-scoping — validated fix; "spec exists on branch" alone false-triggers on repos that persist specs).
- **Task contract:** [[Agent Task File Contract]] — `task_type: dark-factory-implement`, `assignee: github-dark-factory-agent`, `repo`/`clone_url`/`ref`/`pr_number`/`branch`; body is an operator-readable header, the clone is the data source.
- **Downstream:** lands task at `phase: human_review` (never flips the PR). Human flips draft→ready → `github-pr-watcher` → `github-pr-review-agent`.

## Part 4 — Behavior (phases)

| Phase | Impl shape | Reads | Side effects | Writes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| planning | pure-Go spec scan (`agent/code` shape) | frontmatter (`clone_url`,`ref`,`branch`,`pr_number`) | clone branch, precondition checks (ref==HEAD, `.dark-factory.yaml`, approved-not-completed spec, PR draft) | `## Plan` |
| execution | custom step (dark-factory lifecycle + git) | `## Plan` | generate prompts → audit+approve → execute → verify → `spec complete`; commit + push per prompt | `## Result` |
| ai_review | `claudelib.NewAgentStep` (read-only) | `## Plan`+`## Result` | remote checks: all specs `completed`, no prompts in-flight, PR still draft, diff-vs-spec sanity | `## Review`; `phase: human_review`, clear assignee |

**Never runs `gh pr ready`.** The human's flip is the verification sign-off.

## Part 4.2 — ✅ Execution engine dependency (RESOLVED — shipped + live-validated)

The Phase-1 E2E surfaced a hard requirement: **dark-factory spawned nested claude-yolo containers** for the LLM steps. Since this agent's Job pod is *already* a claude-yolo container, that is DinD — disallowed (goal Non-goal).

**Prerequisite SHIPPED (2026-07-13): dark-factory `backend: local`** — a second `pkg/executor.Executor` (`localSubprocessExecutor`) that runs `claude` directly in the current process/cwd instead of `docker run`. Selected via config or `dark-factory run --set backend=local`. Git orchestration stays in the binary unchanged. Landed as spec 104, released **v0.192.0** (docs v0.192.1, scenario 024 v0.192.2). The agent's Dockerfile pins `DARK_FACTORY_VERSION=v0.192.0`.

**Live-validated 2026-07-13** with a real `dark-factory run --set`-style config (`backend: local`, `workflow: direct`, bare-remote sandbox):
- **Happy path:** a real approved prompt → claude ran **in-process (~11s), zero docker containers** → produced the change → `git commit` → prompt `completed`. This is the exact loop the execution step drives.
- **Fail path:** claude absent → fails closed (`claude not found on PATH`), no docker (scenario 024, `active`).

So the agent invokes `dark-factory run` (or per-prompt equivalents) with `--set backend=local` and lets dark-factory's Go binary do git; no nested containers, no DinD.

## Part 5 — Data contract & invariants

- Config via `--set` at runtime, NEVER committed to the PR branch (committed `.dark-factory.yaml` divergence conflicts `workflow:direct`'s `git merge origin/master`). Keep the branch current with `origin/<default>`.
- **★ claude auth is HOME-sensitive (live-smoke finding 2026-07-13).** `backend: local` runs `claude` as a subprocess inheriting the pod's env. If `claude`'s login credential is not discoverable from the process's `HOME`, every prompt fails fast with `Not logged in · Please run /login` (observed: overriding `HOME` broke auth even with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set). **Requirement:** the Job pod MUST provision claude's login where the agent process's `HOME` resolves it — bake/mount the credential into the runtime `HOME` (claude-yolo image convention), do NOT rely on `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` alone. Add a startup precondition check: run a trivial `claude --print` (or reuse dark-factory's claude probe) and fail the task early with a clear escalation if unauthed, rather than failing every prompt.
- **★ the dark-factory Claude PLUGIN must be installed, not just the CLI (E2E root cause 2026-07-13).** backend:local's generation and prompt-audit steps run the slash commands `/dark-factory:generate-prompts-for-spec` and `/dark-factory:audit-prompt` *inside* claude. If the runtime `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` has the CLI binary but not the plugin, claude reports `Unknown command: /dark-factory:generate-prompts-for-spec` → **zero prompts generated → the spec resets to `approved` and the daemon idles at "nothing to do"** (silent — no error surfaces to the agent; looks like a generation-trigger bug but is really a provisioning gap). **Requirement:** the Dockerfile installs the plugin at build time (`claude plugin marketplace add bborbe/dark-factory && claude plugin install dark-factory@dark-factory`, verified with `claude plugin list | grep -q dark-factory`), mirroring github-pr-review-agent's build-time `coding` install. Keep the plugin's minor aligned with `DARK_FACTORY_VERSION`.
- **★ backend:local ignores dark-factory `config.env` (spec-104 gap).** `pkg/executor.localSubprocessExecutor.buildCommand` passes `--model` from config but never sets `cmd.Env` — so the subprocess inherits only the *ambient* process env. Unlike the docker backend (which injects `config.env` into the container), backend:local does NOT apply `env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` / token from `~/.config/dark-factory/config.yaml`. **Requirement:** the Job pod sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (model router) and the auth token as **pod env vars**, not via dark-factory `config.env`. (Follow-up: dark-factory could merge `config.env` into the local subprocess env so one config works for both backends.)
- Agent MUST drive `dark-factory spec complete` (else spec stays `verifying` = approved-not-completed → watcher re-emits).
- Idempotency: `AgentStep.ShouldRun` checks if the phase's `##` section exists; per-prompt commits make execution crash-resumable.
- Concurrency: per-repo cap 1 (Config CRD) — two PRs on one repo must not race git push.

## Part 6 — Operations

- Pattern B Job (not cron); resource profile ~ `github-pr-review-agent`.
- Kill switch: remove/disable the Config CRD.
- Observability: phase-transition logs + metrics; per-prompt execution visible.

## Part 7 — Safety / failure modes

1. **Prompt fails DoD / audit fail** — spec-078 fail-closed stops the spec; agent escalates (clear assignee, `previous_assignee`, phase unchanged). NO auto-fix loop.
2. **Spec has no scenario** — `verify-spec` can't pass; either require a scenario at watcher-emit time, or `spec complete` after prompts (less safety). Decide at build time.
3. **`workflow:direct` git-merge-origin/master conflict** — mitigated by config-via-`--set` + non-divergent branch + pre-run sync.
4. Security: GH token + git-push creds via Secret; PR content visible to claude (acceptable, zero-retention).

### Auto-approve blast radius (accepted)

The execution phase runs dark-factory with `--auto-approve-prompts`. This is the intended bookend design, not a blind approval. The flag triggers dark-factory's spec-078 audit-then-approve: each auto-generated prompt is AUDITED headlessly and approved only if the audit passes (fail-closed — a failing audit stops the spec and the agent escalates). The blast radius is bounded by four independent gates: (a) the human pre-approves the SPEC on the draft PR before the agent runs (first bookend); (b) the spec-078 fail-closed audit gate on every generated prompt; (c) this agent's ai_review diff-vs-spec sanity check before `human_review`; (d) the human's draft→ready flip on the PR (final bookend). The execution pod is single-tenant and ephemeral, so a rogue prompt cannot reach beyond the one PR branch. dark-factory has no per-prompt-id allowlist (`--auto-approve-prompt-ids` does not exist) — the audit gate IS the allowlist.

## Part 8 — Acceptance (per goal SCs)

Deployed in dev, consumes a real watcher task, walks planning→execution→ai_review in one pod, lands at `human_review` without flipping the PR; output parity with the Phase-1 prototype; idempotent under replay; per-repo concurrency 1. ✅ Prerequisite (dark-factory `backend: local`) shipped v0.192.0 and live-validated — the build is unblocked.

## Open decisions

1. ~~Execution engine: build the dark-factory local Executor first~~ — **RESOLVED**: built + shipped as `backend: local` (v0.192.0), live-validated happy + fail paths. The agent drives `dark-factory run --set backend=local`.
2. Scenario-required-or-not for verify (Part 7.2). Leaning: do NOT hard-require a scenario at emit time (spec 104 itself shipped without one, verified by unit tests + the live-smoke); instead the agent runs `spec complete` after prompts pass DoD, and `verify-spec` when a scenario exists. Revisit once the watcher emits real tasks.

func TestCausePrefix(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct{ name, in, want string }{
		{"empty yields unknown", "", "unknown"},
		{"whitespace-only yields unknown", "   ", "unknown"},
		{"first line only", "line one\nline two", "line one"},
		{"trims", "  boom  ", "boom"},
		{"truncates long line", strings.Repeat("a", causePrefixMaxRunes+10), strings.Repeat("a", causePrefixMaxRunes) + "..."},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if got := causePrefix(c.in); got != c.want {
				t.Fatalf("causePrefix(%q) = %q, want %q", c.in, got, c.want)

		})
	}
}

- Source facts are unusually well verified and pinned to exact library versions (`agent@v0.138.0`, `sentry-go@v0.50.0`, `sentry@v1.10.7`), including the non-obvious `NewStacktrace()` capture-time behavior that motivates a fingerprint rather than a message-only fix.

## Summary
This is a well-researched, accurate prompt whose code references all verify against the pinned sources. The main gap is test depth: the Sentry fingerprint is a registry/capture-boundary value, and only the processor transformation is tested — an end-to-end capture test is needed so a wiring regression cannot silently reproduce `NUKE-PROD-CV`. Priority action: add the boundary test (Critical 1), then tighten helper branch coverage (R4) and reconcile the plain-testing choice with `docs/dod.md`/`go-testing-guide.md` (R3).
